body.x: In a lithium-ion battery pack, a fire that starts in one cell can reach its neighbors through ignition and radiant heat, and the space between modules leaves little room for safety equipment.
What if the suppression agent sat between the modules and released once a set temperature was reached?

That is the design of ANT, an ultra-thin automatic fire suppression system from FIREKIMES Co., Ltd., a Cheongju-based company led by CEO Byungyul Kim. At KES 2026, FIREKIMES is presenting ANT to battery and ESS companies and global OEMs and looking for partners to supply it in Korea and abroad.

ANT is installed between battery modules to respond to thermal runaway. It is designed to activate its suppression capsule at a predetermined temperature, lower the temperature at the ignition point, prevent ignition from spreading to surrounding cells and prevent heat propagation caused by radiant heat. The capsule can be made at a volume of 1.0 cm³ or less to minimize installation space, and the system can be customized to the battery type and module specifications. ANT has completed development and is being supplied to customers.

FIREKIMES develops automatic fire suppression systems for electrical equipment and batteries. Its STICK series can be installed in enclosed spaces such as electrical panels, distribution boards and control cabinets, and RED BLOCK is designed for medium- and large-sized electrical equipment. Both detect a rise in temperature and release the suppression agent automatically.

The company reported revenue of KRW 1.6 billion (about USD 1.1 million) in 2025 and KRW 3.1 billion in the first half of 2026, more than the previous full year. It exports to the United States, Mexico, India, Indonesia and Slovakia, has been selected as a G-PASS company, which supports entry into overseas public procurement, and has taken part in ACT Expo, the NFPA Conference & Expo and The Battery Show.

FIREKIMES plans to expand in the United States, where it is going through UL-related procedures, and to enter the Middle East and Europe, working with local battery, ESS and electrical equipment companies and with distributors and agents that can provide technical sales. It cites the cost and time of country-specific certifications and the search for reliable local buyers and agents as its main challenges, and says help with certification costs and buyer matching would contribute most.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
